title: Trading calendar rule set
description: Holiday rules of a stock exchange. Every rule is resolved to concrete dates per year; weekends are never emitted because the trading calendar handles Saturday and Sunday separately.

note.description: Free text explaining sources and known limitations of this calendar. Written for the next person editing these rules; it has no effect on the calculated dates.

authoritativeFrom.description: First year for which this rule set is backed by an authoritative exchange calendar. Asking for closures of an earlier year is rejected rather than answered with a guess. Omit for no lower bound.

authoritativeThrough.description: Last year for which this rule set is backed by an authoritative exchange calendar. Omit for no upper bound.

rules.description: The recurring closures. A rule set that extends another one lists only its deviations here; the inherited rules are evaluated first.

additionalClosures.description: Announced or historical full closures that cannot be expressed safely as a recurring rule, for instance a day of national mourning. These dates are added to the calculated closures.

openDates.description: Dates produced by a rule on which the exchange nevertheless held a trading session. These dates are removed from the calculated closures, which is the only way to cancel a single occurrence of a rule.

dayOfWeek.description: Weekday name in English and upper case.

rule.description: One holiday. Which of the optional fields are required depends on the type; a rule missing a field its type needs is rejected when saving.

name.description: Descriptive name of the holiday, for instance GoodFriday. Appears in the closure preview to explain why a date was calculated, so make it recognisable.

type.description: How the rule is resolved to dates. FIXED: same month and day every year. NTH_WEEKDAY: for instance the third Monday in January. WEEKLY: the same weekday all year. EASTER_RELATIVE / ORTHODOX_EASTER_RELATIVE: an offset in days from Easter Sunday. HIJRI: an Islamic date converted to the Gregorian calendar. EXPLICIT_DATES: a fixed list of dates.

validFrom.description: First year in which the closure applies, inclusive. Essential rather than decorative: Juneteenth became a closure at the US exchanges only in 2021. Omit when the rule was always in force.

validTo.description: Last year in which the closure applies, inclusive. This is also how an inherited rule is switched off from a given year on. Omit when the rule is still in force.

halfDay.description: True when the exchange only shortens its trading hours instead of closing. Such a day is recorded so the rule set describes the exchange completely, but it is never emitted as a closure -- a half day is a trading day.

month.description: Month 1-12. Required for FIXED, NTH_WEEKDAY and HIJRI.

day.description: Day of month. Required for FIXED and HIJRI.

nth.description: Occurrence of the weekday within the month, 1 to 5, or -1 for the last one. Required for NTH_WEEKDAY.

dayOfWeek.description: The weekday selected by a NTH_WEEKDAY or WEEKLY rule.

offset.description: Offset in days from Easter Sunday, negative for dates before it: -2 is Good Friday, 1 Easter Monday, 39 Ascension, 50 Whit Monday. Required for the Easter relative types.

observance.description: How a closure falling on a weekend is transferred. NONE drops it, which is correct wherever holidays are not made up, for instance in Switzerland. Defaults to NONE.

offsetTolerance.description: Days by which the observed Hijri date may deviate from the arithmetic conversion, because the start of an Islamic month depends on the sighting of the moon. A value greater than zero widens the rule to that whole span.

dates.description: The dates of an EXPLICIT_DATES rule.
